{{nihongo|'''Kamuhatori Shrine'''|神服神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Settsu Province]].

'''Kamuhatori Shrine''' (かむはとりじんじゃ; now also read "Shinpuku Jinja") is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in Miyanokawara Motochō, {{ill|Takatsuki|Q335423|qid=Q335423}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and its former rank was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.

===Enshrined deities===
*Hinosuhaya-hi-no-Mikoto - distant ancestor of Mara no Sukune
*Mara no Sukune - ancestor of the {{ill|Hattori no Muraji|ja|服部氏|qid=Q11516960|lt=Hattori no Muraji}}, an {{ill|Isu no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|伊豆国造|qid=Q11380553}} lineage descended from {{ill|amenomihokonomikoto|ja|天御桙命|qid=Q119380365}}
*{{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}

===History===
[[File:Kamihatori02.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Honden]]
To the northwest of the shrine at Tsukawaki, the "Hattori no Muraji mound" and "Meme-zuka" in a {{ill|Kofun|Q1141225|qid=Q1141225}} group are said to be the couple's graves of the Hattori no Muraji. The local Hattori {{ill|Muraji|es|Muraji|ff|Muraji|fr|Muraji|it|Muraji|ja|連|ko|무라지|nl|Muraji|pt|Muraji|ru|Мурадзи|uk|Мурадзі|qid=Q2735611}} had worshiped their ancestral deity there and called it Hattori Shrine, but in the {{ill|Engi (era)|de|Engi (Ära)|fa|انگی (دوره)|fr|Ère Engi|ia|Engi (era)|id|Engi|ja|延喜|ko|엔기|ru|Энги (нэнго)|simple|Engi (era)|sr|Енги (ера)|tr|Engi (dönem)|uk|Енґі (ненґо)|zh|延喜|zh_yue|延喜|qid=Q1374325}} era (901-923) it was renamed Kamuhatori Shrine. In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, it was listed as one of three small shrines of {{ill|Shimakami district|Q10965808|qid=Q10965808}} in {{ill|Settsu Province|Q864163|qid=Q864163}}.

Until the {{ill|維新|cs|Duy tan (rozcestník)|ja|維新|ko|유신|vi|Duy Tân (định hướng)|zh|維新|qid=Q104843054}}, monks of {{ill|Yasuoka-ji|ja|安岡寺 (高槻市)|qid=Q11450605|lt=Yasuoka-ji}} managed shrine affairs. In Meiji 5 (1872), it was ranked {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. In November Meiji 40 (1907), Kasuga Shrine and Inari Shrine from Miyanohara Kawara were moved into the precincts. In the following year, Meiji 41 (1908), Jōgū Shrine of Tsukawaki, Wakamiya Shrine of Uradō, and Shinmei Shrine of Ōzōshi were {{ill|Co-Enshrinement|Q11412524|qid=Q11412524}}<ref>Yoshii Yoshitaka, "Shikinaisha Survey Report Vol. 5" (1977) {{全国書誌番号|78005760}}</ref>. In Heisei 25 (2013), renovation work was completed<ref>[http://blog.seikikensetsu.co.jp/?eid=1422970 Renovation work completed for Kamuhatori Shrine! - Seiki Construction Co., Ltd.] accessed 2019-01-05</ref>.
